findings.failure_scenario: A mutation that fails its first test row wastes computing resources by running the remaining rows sequentially instead of failing fast and allowing parallel evaluation.
findings.summary: check_ci_push_reuse.sh now tests its mutants in parallel while adhering to PUSH_REUSE_FAIL_FAST for early aborts.

findings.failure_scenario: A hung guard can stall the entire job run until an outer runner workflow limit kills it, leaving no trace in the logs of which specific check caused the stall.
findings.summary: guard_tree.sh now limits guards to GUARD_TREE_GUARD_TIMEOUT (default 2400s) and kills processes that exceed it.

findings.failure_scenario: If the process runner terminates the whole job abruptly due to an overarching timeout, logs will be silent on which checks were actively running during the termination.
findings.summary: guard_tree.sh implements a heartbeat that reports which checks are still actively running every GUARD_TREE_HEARTBEAT seconds.

findings.failure_scenario: A daemon spawned by a step could inherit the heartbeat's FIFO writer file descriptor, causing the pipeline runner to wait indefinitely on the heartbeat even after the original step exits.
findings.summary: ci_guard_steps.sh runs a step heartbeat without leaking the FIFO fd to the step (5>&-), ensuring any child daemons do not keep the heartbeat alive.

findings.failure_scenario: If the check script gets killed by a timeout, the fake \"apr serve\" processes spawned inside their own process group would outlive the script and clutter the CI runner.
findings.summary: check_ladder_cells_producer.sh cleans up orphan processes on exit by searching /proc for cmdlines referencing the temporary $WORK directory.
